Subscriber `afterUpdate` now gets entity with changed delete and update date column.

Adds `softDelete`, `getSoftDeletionReturningColumns` methods to `ReturningResultsEntityUpdator` class to get right returning columns and search for entity `withDeleted()`. Resolves bug in `SubjectExecutor` class. Adds tests for the issue.

**Steps to reproduce or a small repository showing the problem:**

I have a LogSubscriber and I'm using the softRemove feature. When softRemove() is called afterRemove is not triggered (I think it should have an afterSoftRemove decorator). I figured out that softRemove triggers update because deleted data column have been changed (That happens). So I tried do identify if the delete data column have changed its value to know if it was a "real" update or a soft remove operation, but it always show the same value:

`
beforeUpdate(event: UpdateEvent<any>): Promise<any> | void {
		console.log(event.databaseEntity.deleted_at);
		console.log(event.entity.deleted_at);
	}
	
afterUpdate(event: UpdateEvent<any>): Promise<any> | void {
        	console.log(event.databaseEntity.deleted_at);
		console.log(event.entity.deleted_at);
}
`

Results in:
`
2020-07-03T20:03:27.168Z
2020-07-03T20:03:27.168Z
2020-07-03T20:03:27.168Z
2020-07-03T20:03:27.168Z

`

Am I missing something?
comments:
> I figured out that softRemove triggers update because deleted data column have been changed (That happens)

To be clear, the trigger to update happens but event.updatedColumns does not show the delete data column

It seems the softRemove and softRecover have just copy/pasted the columns logic from the update event, which really doesn't make much sense. The problem is clear to see here: https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/src/persistence/SubjectExecutor.ts#L216

I think it would be much better to have separate events for soft remove and recover, rather than try to reuse the update events. The current subscribers have no way to understand if an update, a soft remove or recover happened, and I would guess this is more likely the cause of bugs or confusion.
It seems, that the updated_at column returned to the subscriber unchanged either.

@spotykatch i'm using version 0.2.45 and afterSoftRemove alway return entity is undefine

review_comments: Is this line of code the only difference with `update` method? If so, I would like to re-use `update` method to prevent another peace of complex code to be added into the repo... We can make `update` method to accept returning columns if needed.

oh another diff I see is `withDeleted`. Maybe we can add a third parameter to `update`, like `type: "default" | "soft-delete"`. Dunno, better to came up with better names, but having single `update` method is better for sure.

Ok. Got it.
I think `withDeleted` should be used with updates too. So if the entity is changed when soft deleted, it will fire `afterUpdate` event. It will not if there is no `withDeleted`.
